embeddedValue.title: Embedded Value (EV)
embeddedValue.content:
Embedded Value is the standard life-insurer measure of what the business is worth today: Adjusted Net Worth (shareholder net assets) plus the Value of In-Force business (the discounted present value of profits still to emerge from policies already written). It is a different, usually larger, number than book shareholders' equity, because equity under IFRS 17 does not capture the full future profit locked into the existing policy book.

For FWD Group Holdings: EV rose from $5.57bn (FY2024) to $6.95bn (H1 FY2026). The DCF's cross-check section quotes EV per share ($5.43, ANW+VIF basis) and EV equity per share ($7.88) alongside the DCF's own intrinsic value as a sanity check -- the DCF is not derived from EV, but a large, unexplained gap between the two would be a red flag.

What to watch:

  • EV growth versus new business value added plus unwind, net of dividends/capital returned
  • Operating EV variances (assumption changes, experience variances) disclosed separately from new business

newBusiness.title: New business value and CSM
newBusiness.content:
Value of New Business (VNB) is the discounted profit expected from policies sold in the period -- the growth engine of an embedded-value insurer, since in-force EV only grows as fast as new business replenishes it. New Business CSM is the IFRS 17 Contractual Service Margin created by that same new business: the unearned profit that will be released into income over the life of the policies. New Business Margin is VNB divided by APE (Annual Premium Equivalent, see below) -- the profitability of each dollar of new sales.

For FWD Group Holdings: VNB grew from $834m (FY2024) to $945m (FY2025) to $602m in H1 FY2026 alone (vs $506m H1 FY2025); margin improved from 38.6% (FY2025) to 44.7% (H1 FY2026), so growth here is coming with richer, not thinner, margins.

What to watch:

  • VNB growth outpacing or lagging APE growth (margin direction)
  • New Business CSM building the stock of future IFRS 17 profit emergence

ape.title: Annual Premium Equivalent (APE)
ape.content:
APE is the standard life-insurance sales volume measure: 100% of new regular (recurring) premiums plus 10% of new single (lump-sum) premiums, put on a comparable annualized basis. It is the denominator against which New Business Margin and Value of New Business are judged.

For FWD Group Holdings: APE grew from $1.92bn (FY2024) to $2.45bn (FY2025), with H1 FY2026 ($1.35bn) ahead of H1 FY2025 ($1.25bn) -- the top-line sales-volume read, distinct from the IFRS 17 insurance revenue line.

What to watch:

  • APE growth versus VNB growth (are margins holding as volume scales)
  • Mix shift between regular and single premium (changes the quality of APE, not just the level)

solvency.title: Solvency ratio (HK LCSM basis)
solvency.content:
The Local Capital Summation Method (LCSM) solvency ratio is the Hong Kong Insurance Authority's risk-based capital measure: available capital resources divided by the required minimum, expressed as a percentage. It is the regulator's primary signal of whether an insurer can absorb shocks and keep writing business and paying claims.

For FWD Group Holdings: the ratio fell sharply from 265% (FY2025) to 203% (H1 FY2026) per the qualitative analysis -- still comfortably above the Insurance Authority's 100% minimum, but a large one-period compression in the regulatory buffer that is worth tracking against future capital actions (the perpetual securities and dividend decisions both draw on this same buffer).

What to watch:

  • Further declines toward the regulatory minimum
  • Capital actions (perpetual issuance/redemption, dividends) that move the ratio independent of underlying risk

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For FWD Group Holdings Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For FWD Group Holdings Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For FWD Group Holdings Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For FWD Group Holdings Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For FWD Group Holdings Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For FWD Group Holdings Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For FWD Group Holdings Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For FWD Group Holdings Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For FWD Group Holdings Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
